exception_raise: The sender selects this older narrow-code form for `EXCEPTION_DEFAULT` without `MACH_EXCEPTION_CODES`, exporting task/thread ports at the policy-selected flavor. The in-kernel Unix receiver first requires `ux_handler_port`, widens the two codes and delegates to `catch_mach_exception_raise`; a different registered exception server may implement its own receiver. See [exception delivery](../../subsystems/ipc/exception-delivery.md). [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/exception.c#L355).
mach_exception_raise: For default exception behavior, XNU exports control ports in developer mode or for a corpse, otherwise read ports, and sends the wide exception codes. The local Unix receiver verifies its destination, converts the thread port to a read reference and calls `handle_ux_exception`; it consumes the supplied task/thread send rights only on success and always drops the converted thread reference. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ux_handler.c#L130).
exception_raise_state: The `EXCEPTION_STATE` sender obtains architecture state with `thread_getstatus_to_user`, allocates reply-state storage and sends narrow exception codes with a flavor/count. A successful reply is validated through `thread_setstatus_from_user`, except for corpse notification. The local Unix receiver for this state-only form returns `KERN_INVALID_ARGUMENT`; a user exception server supplies the useful receiver. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/exception.c#L298).
mach_exception_raise_state: The `EXCEPTION_STATE` sender obtains architecture state with `thread_getstatus_to_user`, allocates reply-state storage and sends wide exception codes with a flavor/count. The local Unix receiver for this state-only form returns `KERN_INVALID_ARGUMENT`; a user exception server supplies the useful receiver. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/exception.c#L298).
exception_raise_state_identity: The state-and-identity sender exports policy-selected task/thread capabilities as well as old thread state, flavor and narrow codes. A successful reply is imported through architecture/state validation only when the exception is not `EXC_CORPSE_NOTIFY` and the exported thread port is `IKOT_THREAD_CONTROL`; the read-port delivery branch does not import returned state. The in-kernel Unix handler is an invalid-argument stub for this behavior; its presence in the generated exception subsystem does not mean it implements state editing. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/exception.c#L503-L579).

mach_exception_raise_backtrace: Sends an `EXC_CORPSE_NOTIFY` message containing a kcdata/backtrace-object port to eligible live exception endpoints. The sender tries its candidate ports and stops on success or receive-port death. The local Unix receiver returns invalid argument; interpretation of the diagnostic object by another receiver is outside that body. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/exception.c#L646).
UNDAlertCompletedWithResult_rpc: Requires a nonnull reply object with a notification in progress. Under `KERNEL_CF`, raw XML can be decoded into a dictionary; otherwise the callback receives the raw data pointer. Invokes the stored callback, then locks the reply object and clears its in-progress state and notification key. Callback execution precedes that state reset. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L103).
UNDNotificationCreated_rpc: Locks the reply object and accepts the daemon notification key only if the object is not in progress and its old key equals −1; otherwise it returns invalid argument. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L161).
UNDExecute_rpc: `KUNCExecute` obtains a referenced notification-server port, sends the execution path and UID/GID, releases the port and returns the RPC status. An unavailable endpoint returns `MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST`. The user notification daemon's execution and authorization implementation is not present. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L208).
UNDDisplayNoticeSimple_rpc: The local notice wrapper forwards timeout, flags and bounded UI/path strings to the referenced notification daemon and releases that endpoint afterward. There is no response-button output in this notice form. UI presentation and daemon policy are external; the wrapper reports invalid destination when no server port exists. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L225).
UNDDisplayAlertSimple_rpc: The local alert wrapper forwards timeout, flags, presentation strings and button titles to the referenced daemon and supplies a response-flags output. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L256).

[Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L294).

arcade_register_new_upcall: Requires a valid registration object and the arcade service entitlement. While a refresh is in progress, replaces the saved upcall send right under `arcade_upcall_mutex`, consumes the new right and wakes the waiting refresh. Outside that interval it fails, so possession of the registration port alone does not allow arbitrary-time endpoint replacement. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/arcade.c#L148).
fairplayd_arcade_request: The refresh path marks refresh-in-progress, releases an old upcall port, obtains the host fairplayd endpoint and sends the registration capability. Only a successful send reaches its interruptible deadline wait for registration; an invalid endpoint or failed send clears refresh-in-progress without that wait. Concurrent refresh callers instead sleep on the in-progress flag without this explicit deadline. The external daemon must register an upcall through the separate kernel receiver. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/arcade.c#L182-L257).
arcade_upcall: The local bridge sends a `vm_map_copy` path buffer, its length and file offset to the registered validation service and receives `should_kill`. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/arcade.c#L261).

See [port lifecycle](../../subsystems/ipc/ports-and-rights-lifecycle.md). [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_notify.c#L94).

mach_notify_send_once: When a send-once right is disposed, the helper clears reply context and chooses among dead-port release, an in-kernel kobject notification, full-kernel-port release, or an ordinary one-way notification after unlocking. Only the last branch sends this message to a user receiver. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_notify.c#L185).
host_calendar_changed: The local host-notify helper constructs the generated request type for `HOST_NOTIFY_CALENDAR_CHANGE`, detaches eligible live registrations under the notify/port locks, then sends after releasing the list lock. It fills `msgh_id` from the reply-ID table and moves each registered send-once right. Delivery consumes the registration; calendar subscribers must register again as required. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host_notify.c#L203).

telemetry_notification: The local notification helper obtains the host telemetry service port, sends notice flags and releases the right. iocompressionstats_notification: The VFS statistics sender obtains the host compression-statistics service port, sends notice value zero and releases the right; unavailable endpoints cause an early return. mcc_memory_error_notification: The deferred event-notification path obtains the host memory-error endpoint and dispatches the MCC, guarded by `XNU_LOG_MCC` event payload through this message, then releases the send right. A daemon allocation can precede a later local write failure; this is not a single rollback transaction. [Local path](../../../xnu/bsd/vfs/vfs_xattr.c#L1936).

[Local path](../../../xnu/bsd/vfs/vfs_xattr.c#L2041).

mach_test_sync_upcall: Under `DEVELOPMENT || DEBUG`, `task_test_sync_upcall` requires the current task and a valid caller-supplied send port, invokes this synchronous request/reply operation, releases the supplied send right and returns `KERN_SUCCESS` without propagating the upcall result. Other builds return `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. The wrapper does not look up a configured service port; receiver behavior is external to the declaration. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L10223-L10243).
mach_test_async_upcall: Under `DEVELOPMENT || DEBUG`, `task_test_async_upcall_propagation` requires the current task, a valid caller-supplied port and bounded QoS/I/O-tier values. It propagates those attributes to the port, sets send-importance on the current thread around this one-way upcall, then clears it and releases the send right. Attribute-propagation failure returns early; the upcall result itself is not propagated. Other builds return `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; no configured service endpoint is looked up. [Local path](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L10245-L10290).
